dedupe_keys.name: gaia green area inner city agreement business funded tree planting bologna

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes GAIA, the Green Areas Inner-city Agreement of Bologna, Italy, a public-private partnership in which businesses offset their carbon footprint by paying for the purchase and maintenance of city trees, which give shade and evaporative cooling in heatwaves. It supports the city's Adaptation Plan approved in October 2015 under the LIFE+ BLUE AP project, adopted while no national or regional plan existed. Companies use a calculator on the project website to estimate their carbon dioxide and choose a partnership level; the minimum is 200 euros per tree, covering average purchase and maintenance. The LIFE project ran from October 2010 to April 2013 on a budget of 1,202,000 euros, about half from LIFE, and GAIA is now a stable municipal instrument. By April 2016, 1,405 trees had been sold for 281,000 euros, and studies estimated carbon storage for 24 tree species, pollutant removal and cooling. Coverage is the Bologna urban area, with interest from Bari, Sassari and Cagliari. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the GAIA site. Caveats: planting depends on companies' willingness to offset, and cooling figures are general estimates, not site measurements. It illustrates financing of urban green infrastructure for climate adaptation to extreme heat; related records are the Ghent crowdfunding and Paris OASIS case studies.
name: GAIA Green Area Inner-city Agreement, business-funded tree planting (Bologna)
outcomes: 1,405 trees were funded by companies for 281,000 euros by April 2016, and the model was copied by partner companies in other cities.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the City of Bologna
